title: Port City Colombo builds investment momentum across UAE, Oman, and Qatar | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 1 October 2026 00:05
-     - 252

Port City Colombo Delegation meeting with Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion Royal Advisor for Foreign Trade and International Cooperation Pankaj Khimji, and Undersecretary for Commerce and Industry Ghalib bin Saeed bin Majid Al Maamari

Port City Colombo hosted an exclusive investor forum at The St. Regis Abu Dhabi on 25 September 2026, bringing together senior UAE business leaders, investors, and institutional stakeholders for a focused morning of dialogue on Sri Lanka’s investment proposition and the opportunities available within Port City Colombo’s Special Economic Zone. 

The forum formed the centrepiece of a structured seven-day Gulf roadshow spanning Abu Dhabi, Muscat, and Doha — reflecting the sustained and growing interest from the Gulf investment community in Port City Colombo following a series of high-profile engagements across the region throughout 2026.

The roadshow is a direct response to the momentum generated by Port City Colombo’s Gulf outreach program this year, and the specific appetite from Abu Dhabi’s distinct institutional and sovereign investment community for a more focused and substantive engagement with Sri Lanka’s investment proposition.

The Abu Dhabi forum was hosted by the Embassy of Sri Lanka in the United Arab Emirates in collaboration with Port City Colombo. Opening the forum, Ambassador of Sri Lanka to the UAE Prof. Arusha Cooray, spoke to the depth of the bilateral relationship and Port City Colombo’s role within it. “The UAE is Sri Lanka’s largest trading partner in the Middle East and the sixth largest investor in Sri Lanka” she said. “Port City Colombo reflects Sri Lanka’s economic transformation, reform agenda, and ambition to be a serious partner for Gulf investment. For UAE businesses and investors looking to expand into South Asia, Port City Colombo offers a modern, internationally designed platform that is close and familiar in concept, serving as an extension of what already exists in the UAE.” 

Chief Guest DMCC Deputy CEO and Chief Operating Officer Feryal Ahmadi, shared her perspective on the shifting dynamics of global trade and the role free trade zones will play in that evolution. “Research shows that global trade is moving towards South-South — 35% of global trade in the next ten years will be South-South versus 25% for North trade,” she said. “This means that free trade zones in Dubai, Singapore, and Colombo will be extremely important as connectors for businesses moving forward, acting as launchers that enable businesses to access new markets.”

Colombo Port City Economic Commission Chairman Harsha Amarasekera PC, drew a compelling parallel between Abu Dhabi’s rise as a global investment hub and Sri Lanka’s own strategic positioning. 

“Abu Dhabi’s rise as a premier global trading and investment hub is driven by its strategic location at the crossroads of East and West, its massive sovereign wealth, and its progressive regulatory framework,” he said. “In many ways, Sri Lanka shares some of the same strategic advantages, such as its location in the heart of the Indian Ocean and its natural deep-water ports. It is this shared geographic strength that creates a strong foundation for collaboration between our two countries and investors. Port City Colombo is not a mere development project. It is a strategic national initiative designed to position Sri Lanka as a neutral, wholly connected platform for businesses, linking South Asia with the Middle East, Asia, and beyond.” 

Colombo Port City Economic Commission Director General Revan Wickramasuriya provided attendees with an update on Port City Colombo’s investment momentum, noting that the SEZ’s regulatory framework, from its single-window facilitation model and foreign currency-designated operating environment to its investor protection mechanisms and Sharia-compliant finance framework, is purpose-built to meet the expectations of Gulf investors. 

Bringing the formal proceedings to a close, Colombo Port City Economic Commission Director Commercial Radika Obeyesekere, acknowledged the invaluable support extended by the Embassy of Sri Lanka in the UAE in making the forum a success.

Commenting on the significance of Port City Colombo’s Gulf roadshow, CHEC Port City Colombo  Ltd., Managing Director Xiong Hongfeng said: “The depth of engagement we have seen across this roadshow — from Muscat to Abu Dhabi to Doha — reflects a growing recognition among Gulf investors that Port City Colombo offers a credible and familiar platform for accessing South Asia’s growth story. We look forward to translating these conversations into concrete investment partnerships.”

The Abu Dhabi forum was preceded by a series of high-level bilateral meetings in Muscat, where the Port City Colombo delegation engaged with senior representatives of Khazaen Economic City, the Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OCCI), and the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion. 

The delegation met with Khazaen Economic City CEO Eng. Salim bin Suleiman Al Thuhli, Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry Chairman Sheikh Faisal bin Abdullah Al Rawas and Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion Royal Advisor for Foreign Trade and International Cooperation Pankaj Khimji and Director of Khimji Ramdas, together with Undersecretary for Commerce and Industry Ghalib bin Saeed bin Majid Al Maamari. 

Building on the strong foundation established through Port City Colombo’s Muscat investor forum in June 2026 and the subsequent reciprocal delegation visit to Port City Colombo in August, discussions focused on bilateral trade and investment opportunities, the Oman–South Asia investment and trade corridor, and pathways for Omani businesses and institutions to establish a presence within Port City Colombo’s SEZ framework.

The roadshow concluded in Doha with a significant meeting with Qatar Chamber of Commerce and Industry First Vice Chairman Mohamed bin Ahmed bin Twar marking an important step in further strengthening Port City Colombo’s engagement with Qatar’s business and investment community. The fruitful discussion was facilitated by the Embassy of Sri Lanka in the State of Qatar and led by Ambassador of Sri Lanka to Qatar Sithara Khan.

The delegation also held dedicated discussions with senior Embassy officials and engaged with senior representatives of the Qatar–Sri Lanka Business Council, the Sri Lanka Coordinating Committee (SLCC), and the Sri Lanka Business and Professional Council (SLBPC).

Together, these high-level engagements further deepened Port City Colombo’s ongoing outreach in Qatar, strengthening institutional and business relationships and creating new avenues for sustained dialogue, collaboration and cross border investment ties.

title: Keells marks 35 years of keeping life fresh for Sri Lanka | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 1 October 2026 00:04
-     - 84

For Keells, freshness has always meant more than what reaches a supermarket shelf. It represents a commitment built over 35 years to improving everyday experiences, strengthening communities and creating opportunities for the people connected to its journey.

As Keells surpasses its 150th outlet milestone, reflecting on a journey where freshness has always been more than what reaches the shelf; it is reflected in the way Keells supports people, strengthens communities and creates better everyday experiences. From empowering farmers and employees to connecting families with fresh choices, Keells has continued to bring this belief to life through freshness, convenience, trust and care, improving the quality of life for the nation. It is not a new promise, but an outlook that has guided Keells from the very beginning.

Since opening its first store at Liberty Plaza, Colombo in 1991, Keells has evolved alongside changing consumer needs, moving beyond traditional retail to create a connected ecosystem that supports customers, farmers, suppliers, employees, and communities. Today, with 150 stores across Sri Lanka, the brand continues to build on its purpose of improving the quality of life for the nation.w

For customers, this journey is reflected in the everyday choices and experiences Keells continues to create. From farm-fresh produce and prepared food offerings to an expanding range of products, new food experiences and digital innovations such as the Keells Nexus App, the brand continues to evolve around the changing needs of Sri Lankan households. The Nexus ecosystem now connects with 2.9 million members, offering a more personalised and accessible omnichannel experience through relevant promotions, personalised offers and exclusive rewards.

Beyond sourcing fresh produce, Keells continues to invest in strengthening the farming ecosystem. Over 2,000 farmers, including female agripreneurs have been trained in financial literacy, climate-resilient agriculture, organic farming and sustainable cultivation, while model farms and new agricultural technologies support farmers in improving productivity and reducing losses. 

At the heart of Keells’ freshness journey are the farmers who make it possible. Working with over 4,000 active farmers across 10 collection centres, Keells has built a direct sourcing network that connects agricultural communities with consumers across the country. Through initiatives such as Govi Diriya, farmers receive support in climate-resilient agriculture, sustainable cultivation and Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) certification, along with awareness and precautionary measures to prepare for challenges such as El Niño.

With over 6,500 employees, the organisation continues to create opportunities through training, career development and wellbeing initiatives. Through partnerships such as NAITA certification, Keells supports employees in building recognised skills and progressing in their careers. This is complemented by initiatives that support employees through different stages of their lives, including leadership development and career growth for women through She Rises, access to mental and social wellbeing support through Peace Pod, and practical guidance on managing personal finances through the Financial Wellbeing Program.

The commitment extends beyond stores into the wider communities Keells serves. Through initiatives such as pre-school meal programs, food redistribution efforts and youth development programs, Keells continues to create shared value. The pre-school meal initiative has provided over 538,000 meals to more than 4,500 children across 116 pre-schools, while the Skill Into Progress (SKIP) program, organised by the John Keells Foundation and The Rainbow Institute, Keells has supported 1,322 students across 10 locations islandwide, with 280 graduates earning certification, with further rollouts on the horizon.

As Keells looks towards the future, it continues to build on an outlook shaped by years of supporting people, strengthening communities and creating better everyday experiences. Now, Keells hopes to inspire Sri Lankans to find freshness in the little things they do, discover new possibilities and make everyday life a little better.

Because keeping life fresh is not only about what we bring home. It is about the opportunities we create, the communities we strengthen, the better tomorrow we help build together, and how we inspire everyone to live in a fresh way.

title: Budget 2027 to be presented on 12 Nov.; final vote on 14 Dec. | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 1 October 2026 00:03
-     - 56

The President, in his capacity as Finance Minister, will present the 2027 Budget in Parliament on 12 November, 2026, Parliament said. The final vote is scheduled for 14 December.

The timetable was approved by the Committee on Parliamentary Business, chaired by Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne, on 25 September.

The Appropriation Bill for 2027, which sets out Government spending for the year, will be presented for its First Reading on 7 October. The Budget Speech, which marks the Bill’s Second Reading, will be followed by a seven-day debate from 13 to 20 November, with the vote at 6 p.m. on 20 November.

The Committee Stage, where Parliament debates allocations ministry by ministry, will run for 19 days from 21 November to 14 December. The Third Reading vote, which concludes the Budget process, is set for 6 p.m. on 14 December.

The Government will receive 60% of debate time during the Second Reading, with the Opposition receiving 40%. The split reverses during the Committee Stage.

Parliament will sit every day during the Budget period, including Saturdays, except Sundays and public holidays. Budget debates will run from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. each sitting day.

If a division, or recorded vote, is called on a ministry’s expenditure head during the Committee Stage, it will be held at 6 p.m. at the end of that day’s proceedings, according to the Parliament Secretary General.

title: Resus Energy bids for  16 MW of battery storage | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 1 October 2026 00:02
-     - 76

Resus Energy PLC has bid to add 16 MW of battery storage to its existing solar plants, the company said, as it seeks a slice of a 150 MW tender for storage systems attached to the country’s ground-mounted solar farms.

Two subsidiaries, Resus Solar Ltd., and Resus Eastern Solar Ltd., submitted proposals under the Limited Competitive Bidding process for the establishment of 150 MW AC/600 MWh Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). Such systems store electricity generated by solar panels and release it to the grid when needed, including after sunset.

The company said its price bids were within the qualifying price range.

Resus Solar, a fully owned subsidiary, has proposed 14 MW/56 MWh of capacity. Resus Eastern Solar, fully owned by Resus Solar and thus indirectly by the listed parent, has proposed 2 MW/8 MWh. Together, the bids amount to 16 MW/64 MWh, or just over a tenth of the capacity on offer. The megawatt-hour figures imply storage of about four hours at full output.

The equity requirement for the projects is currently estimated at Rs. 650 million to Rs. 800 million, depending on the debt-to-equity ratio, the company said.

Resus Energy said that the projects remain subject to the relevant approvals process and that the bids should not be read as awards. It said further announcements would follow upon receipt of Letters of Award.

title: Storex Renewables partners world’s no. 1 Sigenergy to answer Sri Lanka’s solar policy shift | Daily FT

Storex Renewables Ltd., has launched SigenStor Neo, an all-in-one solar and battery storage system from Sigenergy, in Sri Lanka. The only scalable and future-proof solution comes as the Ministry of Energy moves all new rooftop solar connections to the Net Plus scheme, closing Net Metering and Net Accounting to new applicants. 

With the closure of practically available solar schemes, consumers are now required to have their own storage and be independent in their solar power generation, making on-site storage more valuable for maximising self-consumption and controlling costs. Storex Renewables, which brings prior experience implementing large-scale battery systems, positions SigenStor Neo as its answer to that shift.

Sigenergy Neo Systems integrate the energy management system, inverter, battery and backup module into a single unit. It connects to existing solar installations, so homeowners and businesses already on Net Metering or Net Accounting can add storage without replacing their current setup. The battery is rated for 10,000 charge cycles, the highest count in the market. It carries an IP66 rating for protection against dust and weather exposure in Sri Lankan conditions. The Sigenergy inverter is perhaps the first available in stock in Sri Lanka that can grow with your demand. Whilst traditional battery-based solar systems do not offer future upgradability of batteries of different sizes during different stages, Storex offers a premium future-proof solution. The Storex Sigenergy system switches to backup power with zero disruption to connected loads, and allows power to be drawn efficiently from panels installed at different angles or orientations.

The product is available for both residential and commercial installations with all leading installers such as SOLAR THERM, AIRO Engineering and selected partners/resellers. 

Sigenergy Regional Manager Marvin Xiao said, “We were looking for the best partner to distribute our products in Sri Lanka. We found that partner in Storex.”

Storex Renewables Director Lasith Wimalasena said, “As part of the Windforce PLC Family, we have over two decades of experience in renewable energy and have delivered the largest battery and solar projects in the market. SigenStor Neo will not be just another product on the shelf. It is a premium product integrated and genuinely easy to use, and that is what we are bringing to Sri Lankan homes and businesses.” 

Further elaborating on the subject, Storex Renewables Manager Praboda Welagedera explained that “This is the only solution of its kind fully integrated with inverter, battery and solar, where customers have peace of mind in terms of installation or compatibility issues. It simply works with any existing solar installation as an internal capacity enhancement with battery storage that can also grow.”

In a milestone achievement for Sri Lankan specialty tea, Aratenna Special Silver Tips from Glen Nevis Plantation in the historic Kandy region has been named the Overall Gold Medal Winner at the 2026 North American Tea Conference, organised by the Tea and Herbal Association of Canada.

This prestigious international accolade celebrates the pinnacle of craftsmanship, delicate flavor, and exceptional terroir that defines Ceylon specialty white tea.

title: Akram Cassim re-elected SLGJA President for third term | Daily FT

Akram Cassim

Akram Cassim was re-elected President of the Sri Lanka Gem and Jewellery Association (SLGJA) for a third term at the Association’s Annual General Meeting held recently.

The AGM also elected a new Board representing a strong mix of youth and experience, bringing together members from across the gem, jewellery and lapidary sectors and from key gem and jewellery regions of Sri Lanka.

Joining Cassim in the new leadership team are Shezan Mansoor as Vice President and COO; Shezard Careem as Head of the Jewellery Segment; Razni Haniffa as Head of the Gem Segment; Amanda Wijemanne as Head of the Lapidary Segment; Shezmin Munsoor as Head of Promotions and FACETS; and Nawrooz Azmi as Head of Finance.

Cassim said he was delighted with the composition of the new Board and its broad representation across the industry.

 “We have a well-balanced Board combining experience with a new generation of industry leaders, representing the different sectors and regions that make up Sri Lanka’s gem and jewellery industry. I believe this gives us a strong team to address the challenges before us, bring fresh ideas to the table and take the industry forward together.”

In his address to the AGM, Cassim highlighted industry reform as a key priority, including continued engagement with the Industry Ministry, NGJA, EDB, Customs and other relevant authorities on tax, fiscal and regulatory matters. He noted the progress made on the importation of rough gemstones while identifying the liberalisation of gold imports as an important next step in supporting jewellery manufacturing and value-added exports.

He also highlighted the continued development of FACETS Sri Lanka, traceability, gem and jewellery tourism and greater participation by the younger generation as priorities for the Association.

Looking ahead to FACETS Sri Lanka 2027, its 34th edition, Cassim called on the entire industry to support the exhibition by bringing international buyers and sponsors to Sri Lanka and using their global networks to further strengthen the show. He also welcomed Gübelin Gem Lab as an official partner of FACETS 2027.

With the SLGJA marking its 25th anniversary next year, Cassim said the milestone was an opportunity to celebrate the Association’s achievements while setting an ambitious direction for the future.

“We have a proud heritage, a remarkable industry and tremendous potential. With confidence, ambition and shared purpose, we can strengthen Sri Lanka’s position on the world stage.”

He summed up the Association’s direction for the year ahead in three words: “One industry, one vision, one voice.”

title: World Bank approves $ 110 m for 600km of climate-resistant roads in Sri Lanka | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 1 October 2026 00:00
-     - 46

The World Bank yesterday approved $ 110 million to help Sri Lanka repair and reconstruct 600 kilometers of roads that were severely damaged by Cyclone Ditwah.

 The new financing, provided through the International Development Association’s Crisis Response Window, will prioritise roads that restore access to markets, schools, and health facilities in the communities most severely affected by the cyclone. 

Reconstructed roads will be built to climate-resilient standards incorporating improved drainage systems, landslide protection measures, and updated engineering to withstand extreme weather events that are becoming more frequent and severe, the World Bank said.

 “Cyclone Ditwah has had a devastating impact on connectivity across Sri Lanka, but rebuilding also gives us an opportunity to build back stronger,” said World Bank Group Country Manager for Sri Lanka Gevorg Sargsyan. “This is about more than fixing roads. It is about restoring livelihoods, reconnecting farmers to markets and families to essential services, and ensuring that the infrastructure rebuilt today is resilient enough to withstand future shocks.”

This new financing extends the ongoing Inclusive Connectivity and Development Project (ICDP) by three years, bringing total World Bank investment in Sri Lanka’s transport connectivity under the operation to $ 610 million.

The investment is expected to directly benefit more than 830,000 people, with close to two million people reached across eight target districts. The investment is also expected to create roughly 5,671 new or improved jobs in reconstruction and maintenance activities, and benefit close to 22,000 tea, vegetable, and paddy farmers by reconnecting them to buyers and supply chains.  

Cyclone Ditwah struck the island in November 2025, causing an estimated $ 4.1 billion in damages and affecting nearly two million people across all 25 districts. The transport sector sustained approximately $ 973 million in damages, including close to 2,000 kilometers of provincial roads, more than 3,500 kilometers of rural roads, and close to 700 bridges, with recovery needs estimated at $ 1.31 billion.

The project is aligned with the World Bank Group’s Country Partnership Framework for Sri Lanka for 2026–2030, which identifies resilient infrastructure and connectivity as foundations for recovery and private sector-led growth.

title: FAAMA appoints new Executive Committee for 2026/27, targeting  $ 1 b local value-addition opportunity | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 1 October 2026 00:00
-     - 46

FAAMA Chairman Husni Salieh

The Fabric and Apparel Accessory Manufacturers Association (FAAMA) has reappointed Husni Salieh of Noyon Lanka Ltd., Chairman for the 2026/27 term at its Annual General Meeting held on 25 September 2026 at the Hilton Colombo.

The AGM was graced virtually by Board of Investment of Sri Lanka Chairman Duminda Hulangamuwa as Chief Guest, and Export Development Board Chairman Mangala Wijesinghe in person as Guest of Honour.

The event brought together FAAMA members, industry leaders and government representatives providing an opportunity to reflect on the Association’s achievements and discuss priorities for the year ahead.

FAAMA is a member association of the Joint Apparel Association Forum (JAAF), the apex body representing Sri Lanka’s apparel industry. JAAF Chairman Felix Fernando congratulated the new Chair and said: “I am confident that the new leadership will help strengthen Sri Lanka’s local fabric and accessories supply chain and drive the industry towards our 2030 goals.” 

Reviewing the year, Salieh said that Sri Lanka’s Fabric and Apparel Accessory industry contributes an estimated $ 800 million to $ 1 billion in export revenue as part of Sri Lanka’s $ 5 billion apparel and textile exports. A significant share of raw materials is still imported.

“There is a billion-dollar opportunity for more locally sourced raw materials as apparel in the country looks to grow from $ 5 billion to $ 8 billion by 2030,” he said. “Many of the challenges our industry faces cannot be addressed by any one company, association or institution working independently. They require a collective industry response.”

Over the past year FAAMA has been working with JAAF, the BOI and the EDB on a common apparel strategy towards 2030. It held closed-door sessions with leading apparel manufacturers and ran seminars on tax and export regulations. It also worked with the Vocational Training Institute on building technical skills. Members’ concerns, including the abolition of SVAT and foreign currency payment thresholds, were raised with the President, the BOI and the EDB.

EDB Chairman Mangala Wijesinghe said apparel accounts for more than 30% of Sri Lanka’s exports, with nearly $ 5.5 billion in apparel exports. Exports have softened this year on weaker global demand linked to the Middle East conflict, but the EDB projects average export growth of around 7% and GDP growth of around 6%.

The EDB pointed to textile imports of nearly $ 2.7 billion as an opening for local producers. “If we can support these industries, we can save a lot of foreign exchange and strengthen the sector,” the representative said.

On tightening EU rules, the EDB acknowledged higher compliance costs, particularly for SMEs. “If Sri Lankan exporters use international standards, with circularity, low-carbon production and better traceability, we can differentiate ourselves from competitors and gain strong market access,” he added. 

In a video message, while congratulating the new executive committee, BOI Chairman Duminda Hulangamuwa said the industry’s vertical integration is a strategic advantage. “We have integrated vertically, with fabric and accessories manufacturers supplying the entire value chain,” he said. He added that the BOI aims to work closely with FAAMA to raise local sourcing from where it’s at currently and will meet the new committee soon to expedite this.

The re-elected Chairman said: “We have spent a lot of time understanding the challenges. Now, it’s time to move towards collective action,” and urged members to embrace change. He recalled the well-known quote, “It’s not the strongest or the fastest of the species that survives, but those most adaptable to change,” and highlighted that this is very much a moment of change for FAAMA and the rest of our industry.

The office bearers for 2026/27 are Husni Salieh of Noyon Lanka Ltd., as Chairman; Niroshan Samarasinhe of Stretchline Ltd., and Shahid Sangani of Dynawash Ltd., as Vice Chairmen; Shehan Olegasageram of Compreli Consulting Ltd., as Secretary; and Suranga Gallage of Antler Fabric Printers Ltd., as Treasurer. 

They will be joined on the Executive Committee by Janaka Nanayakkara of Teejay Lanka PLC, Harin Gabriel of American & Efird Ltd., Jonah Goh of Best Pacific Textiles Lanka Ltd., Beauno Fernando of Shore to Shore Ltd., Ruwan Mudalpath of Ocean Lanka Ltd., Yasantha Suriyapperuma of Wilkins Spence Packaging Lanka Ltd., and Vasu Wijegoonawardane of Prym Intimates Lanka Ltd.

The Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court yesterday fixed 11 November for the next hearing of the case against Ex-President Ranil Wickremesinghe and former Presidential Secretary Saman Ekanayake, pending the Attorney General’s advice.

The case, filed by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), concerns the alleged misuse of about Rs. 16.9 million in public funds. The money relates to Wickremesinghe’s attendance at his wife’s graduation ceremony in London during an official visit to the US and the UK in late 2023.

Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena issued the order after considering the progress of the investigations. Both Wickremesinghe and Ekanayake were present in court.

The CID arrested Wickremesinghe on 22 August, 2025, and he was remanded until 26 August, the first time a former Sri Lankan head of state had been placed in remand custody. He was later released on three personal bail bonds of Rs. 5 million each after medical reports were submitted.

title: Hambantota women stage awareness protest in Colombo for Tobacco-Free Generation | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 1 October 2026 00:00
-     - 27

Over 300 women and mothers assembled outside the Presidential Secretariat last week  demanding immediate Government action for the introduction and implementation of the proposed ‘Tobacco-Free Generation’ (TFG) policy in the country.

Organised by the Hambantota Women’s Development Federation (WDF), this gathering brought together women from various parts of the Hambantota District. This peaceful demonstration was held outside the Presidential Secretariat and culminated in the delegation presenting a request to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, with almost 10,000 signatures, showing their support to urge the introduction of the TFG policy in order to safeguard the children of Sri Lanka from the harms of tobacco use.

TFG is a globally recognised public health framework that seeks to permanently phase out smoking. This proposal would ban the sale of all tobacco products to children born in or after 2010 which ensures that children turning 21 in 2031 will never legally be able to purchase tobacco. It was formally proposed to the Health Minister on two occasions by the Sri Lanka Medical Association (SLMA) in 2024 and 2025. In 2026, the National Authority on Tobacco and Alcohol (NATA) along with the SLMA once again submitted the proposal to introduce the TFG policy in Sri Lanka to the Minister. However, the proposal remains to be submitted to the Cabinet for approval. 

The women of the South gathered to make their voices heard on the enactment of the TFG proposal, undeterred by the adverse weather conditions currently impacting the island.

title: Opposition’s strategic dilemmas, Easter massacre matrix | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 1 October 2026 00:24
-     - 148

First understand the masterplan, then connect the dots to discern the mastermind

SJB 24 Sept.: spectacular solo achievement, tactical victory

Sajith at Polduwa: Undeniable success, but could be more inclusive

An opinion poll in the Sunday Times (27 Sep.) on the 2nd anniversary of AKD-NPP rule shows 58% dissatisfaction and only 42% satisfaction. This means that President Dissanayake has retained the vote—below an absolute majority—that brought him into office, but that the JVP-NPP’s high popularity at the Parliamentary election has been reduced to the same level as his, while he hasn’t increased his popularity either.

The 58% negative vote should gladden the Opposition, but it really can’t because the Opposition contains a bipolar split between Sajith/SJB and Namal/SLPP. Namal may have run the gruelling legal gauntlet by Presidential election 2029. 

There are only two scenarios/templates in the playbook which can break the Opposition stalemate in 2029:

I. Sajith emulates his father’s 1988 breakthrough victory beating the formidable Sirimavo Bandaranaike by swinging the poor among SLFP voters and JVP supporters through the inspiring vision of Janasaviya, the radical poverty-reduction program. 

II. Namal combines and emulates CBK’s 1994 repositioning of her party and 1999 defeat of Ranil, and his father’s patriotic-populist 2005 victory over Ranil.

UNP-SP-SJB

The UNP fails to recognise that its decades-long inability to elect a President to lead the country was because it de-Premadasaised its economic ideology post-1993, and failed to transition over a decade ago to Sajith as leader. 

There is no bigger indictment of the UNP and the pro-Ranil caucus in the SJB than the electorate’s verdict on ‘unmandated’ President Wickremesinghe who was consigned to third place in 2024 having ‘saved the country’. 

Sajith Premadasa probably hasn’t forgotten that Ranil dragged his feet and defeated him in 2019, ran as spoiler and defeated him in 2024, and only succeeded in getting Anura Dissanayake and the JVP-NPP elected as our rulers. 

Namal is rightly allergic – for ideological ‘brand’ reasons – to any alliance with Ranil’s UNP (hence the latter’s Anuradhapura absence). 

The UNP has no successor to Ranil. The party can avoid electoral-political extinction only if it recognises Sajith as leader/candidate  and enters an equation with the SJB as main force. That’s the last move with which Ranil can redeem himself and be assured of respectful recognition and status.

The rest of the Joint Opposition including the SLFP should recognise Namal as leader/candidate, abandoning delusions of a non-Sajith/non-Namal candidate with a mass base, national resonance and double-digit viability.

SJB post-Polduwa

Sajith Premadasa and the SJB scored a significant tactical and symbolic victory with their impressive ‘swarm’ demonstration, over 5000-strong, at Polduwa on 24 September, proving the SJB’s dominant status within the Opposition. 

That victory was more limited than it might have been, and had an avoidable downside, because of an arrogant, disruptive streak on the part of some overtly right-wing SJB organisers/MPs—notorious loose cannon—exhibiting sectarianism, isolationism and unilateralism. 

To succeed and prevail, Sajith and the SJB should treat five strategic political realities as fundamentals: 

1. A ‘One-Party State’ project cannot be defeated by a mirroring ‘One-Party Opposition’ project and posture. It can only be defeated by a broad, politically pluralist democratic project with social democracy at the core.   

2. The SJB which since its inception failed twice (2020, 2024) to break out of its parent/predecessor UNP’s 20% electoral bunker, cannot afford to risk going it alone, not least in a three-way race. It must win over the middle-ground, the swing voters and new voters, to constitute a majority. 

3. The interests of the whole must, in general, supersede the interests of the part, and the leading part can succeed only if it incorporates and represents the interests of the whole. 

4. Sajith Premadasa is SJB leader and Opposition Leader, and as such must lead, include and represent the interests of the whole Opposition—not just one (albeit biggest) component, his own party, though axiomatically that would be primary. 

5. The SJB is the main and leading Opposition party and must be recognised as such, but it does not hold a monopoly of the Oppositional space. SJB primacy must not translate into exclusivity or self-quarantine. To lead, the SJB must draw in others who follow; form alliances, blocs, partnerships; act in unison or coordination with diverse parties on common issues against a common authoritarian adversary. 

3 Oct.: Resistance reboots 

The 22nd Amendment battle dispelled the ridiculous though widespread illusion that Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya was an enlightened liberal dissident and potential counterweight within the AKD Cabinet and JVP-NPP Parliamentary group. 

She mounted a wall-to-wall defence of the amendment, and pronounced harshly on her uncle, Prof. G.L. Peiris—though the English language provided for less rude, insolent judgmentalism and more finesse and civility. Prof. G.L. Peiris’ detailed critique of 22A did not come from his Ministerial past which she finds so reprehensible, but from his stellar scholarly side. 

Comrade Minister Bimal Rathnayake’s announcement that the Government will not seek to enter a successor IMF program after the current one expires in 2027,  leaves me suspicious about what he doesn’t say: that the Government will not re-enter the international money markets in 2027. The recourse to the high-interest global money markets as distinct from bilateral and multilateral funding and foreign direct investment is the crux of our crisis. 

The Protection of the State From Terrorism Bill which has just been gazetted, is significantly worse than the Prevention of Terrorism Act it replaces. The new Bill’s ambit is wider than armed actions, their organisation or intent to commit them. There’s no such animal as ‘unarmed terrorism’, but going by the Bill’s expansive language, Anura thinks there is. This is not a Bill to ‘protect the State from Terrorism’ but to pre-emptively protect State Terrorism deployed against unarmed people’s protests and criticism.   

Resistance resumes in the form of the Jana Aragala Vyaparaya mobilisation at Campbell Park on 3 October against unaffordable taxation. Wasantha Mudalige, Aragalaya hero, issued a convincing clarion call: (https://www.facebook.com/share/v/19qxeLyCcp/)

Easter massacre masterplan

Reconstruct the masterplan, and connect the dots to discern the mastermind/s.

The conviction by the court of those most closely involved in the Easter Sunday massacre is welcome but is only half the story and does not—cannot—complete the search for justice.

The verdict deals with ‘sins of commission’—those who assisted or played some role in the Easter massacre by their active involvement. But there were also ‘sins of omission’. Evil was committed not only by those who blew up the innocent and those who assisted them along the way, but also by those who had been informed that the evil deed would happen and chose to do nothing about it, or dragged their feet with the result that a preventable atrocity was not prevented.

In a superb piece of investigative reportage, the Jaffna Monitor reconstructs the story of the 17-day delay.

‘…India’s warning to the State Intelligence Service arrived on April 4, 2019, followed by further information on April 18 and 19; on the evening of the 20th and again at first light on the 21st, the head of the SIS passed his own warnings to the inspector general of police and the defence secretary… 

… On April 4, the warning arrived in Colombo through official channels, as a WhatsApp message to Nilantha Jayawardena, the director of the State Intelligence Service. Zahran Hashim and his associates were preparing a suicide attack on important churches…Six men were named, Zahran and his brother Rilwan among them. The message was confirmed in writing at nine the following morning, and a second Indian source sent the same substance three hours later. 

…On April 7 a top-secret letter reached Sisira Mendis, the Chief of National Intelligence. It set out the same warning and added the methods the group might use: a suicide attack, an armed attack, a knife attack, an attack with a truck. 

On April 8 the defence secretary was told, and advised that the police be informed. 

On April 9 the security chiefs met. That same day Jayawardena sent the inspector general of police a report identifying four of the six men India had named. 

…Then, on April 20, the Indian counterpart messaged Jayawardena again. He wanted feedback on what he had sent at the start of the month. He added that the attack was expected “at any time on or before 21.04.2019,” and that a dry run had already been carried out at Kattankudy. 

That was the same evening a former Sea Tiger in Puthukudiyiruppu took a call from an Indian police officer and relayed the warning to his handler in Vavuniya. 

The last message came at 8.27 the next morning. It said the attackers would probably move within hours. The first bomb went off eighteen minutes later…’ 

(https://www.jaffnamonitor.com/the-long-warning-inside-the-intelligence-trail-that-preceded-easter-bombings/)

As respected author of several books on the LTTE war, MR Narayan Swamy has underscored: 

‘…It is by now public knowledge that an Indian agency passed on highly credible intelligence which, had it been acted upon, could not only have failed the murder conspiracy but also led to the arrests of the bombers. Sadly, the inputs received were not followed up. No amount of planning by the terrorists and no amount of overt or covert help they allegedly received from anyone within Sri Lanka or outside could have succeeded in killing people en masse if the warnings had been heeded…’

(https://www.jaffnamonitor.com/easter-bombings-is-about-inaction-despite-specific-warnings/)

Ian Fleming wrote in Goldfinger, “Once is coincidence, twice is happenstance, three times is enemy action”. 

It wasn’t just one person who ignored or delayed in acting on the Indian intelligence alerts. It was several. They all worked for the State, in similar or related agencies. They belonged to broadly the same category of occupation. If it was only one officer it could have been coincidental, but the chain or clustering suggests conspiracy. 

Why did several intelligence officers behave in the same way, which overrode their training, experience and instincts? Where could they have  caught the ‘delay disease’ from? 

Their names are all known from previous inquiries. Suresh Sallay isn’t one of them. His name seems only to crop up in Azad Maulana’s clip in the TV program. Is he a scapegoat or red herring? He has the wrong profile--not have enough seniority and personal authority to be the mastermind; too junior, youthful, lightweight. Shouldn’t the mastermind have been a heavyweight; some former covert operations chieftain committed to a certain political outcome, who once had authority over them all; someone who remained and remains in the shadows? 

The Saudi/Gulf funded Wahhabi buildup in Eastern Sri Lanka dates back at least to 2012 (https://www.jaffnamonitor.com/the-easter-bombings-did-not-begin-on-easter-sunday/) but there were no bloody attacks on Sinhala targets for several years after that. Organised Islamophobia arose from 2012, through the Bodhu Bala Sena (BBS) and other similar—more vicious-- organisations, ferociously inciting animosity towards Muslim enterprises and communities which resulted in violence, NOT in the East but in the South where there was no such Wahhabi dominance. 

These unprovoked attacks on Muslim targets outside the East by extremist ethnoreligious majoritarian groups, gave the opening for Zahran Hashim to discuss, train for and plan violent attacks on Sinhala targets in the country at large. 

Perhaps these were two prongs of one plot, or consecutive steps up the escalation ladder: 

(a) Create or encourage the creation of Islamophobic Sinhala-Buddhist extremist organisations and discourse and provoke the Eastern Wahhabi fundamentalists to shift focus from exercising cultural domination over Eastern Muslims, to targeting the Sinhala people. 

(b) Ignore the information about the Zahran network and the terrorist build-up, and divert attention to the non-existent LTTE.

(c) Allow the attacks to happen against Sinhala Christian sites and worshippers.

(d) By-pass and override the Cardinal’s successful attempts to stop an anti-Muslim backlash, and enhance an anti-Muslim backlash outside the areas where Christians were a majority or significant minority, in Sinhala-Buddhist majority areas, though the Sinhala-Buddhists hadn’t been targets—thus rousing a tsunami of Sinhala-Buddhist ultranationalism.

(e) Use that ultranationalism as ramp to enable the Sinhala-Buddhist extremist candidate to catapult to the candidacy and victory. 

The respected Israeli newspaper Haaretz has blown the whistle on Prime Minister Netanyahu in a report that has yet to be refuted or criminally prosecuted, stating that the President of the UAE informed Netanyahu of the coming attack by Hamas and Islamic Jihad, 10 days before October 7th but that Netanyahu failed to pass on the warning to Israeli intelligence heads including of Shin Bet! Earlier the BBC had reported that the head of Egyptian Intelligence had passed on a similar warning to Netanyahu days before Oct 7th and it too had been ignored.  

Could it because Netanyahu was elected to office the first time around in 1996, when he was running behind in the race with Leah Rabin in the aftermath of the assassination of her husband, peace-making Prime Minister Itzhak Rabin, by a Jewish extremist who hated the Oslo Accords—and Netanyahu won only because a Hamas bomb exploded on a bus just before the election? 

Israeli organisations staffed by ex-covert ops specialists have played an insidious role in electoral processes the world over. The Guardian (UK) ran a story with the following headline and ‘strap’: 

‘France accuses Israeli firm of interfering in Scottish elections and targeting SNP.

Cyber agency says BlackCore targeted John Swinney, as well as interfering in New York and French elections.’

(https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/jun/12/france-accuses-israeli-firm-interfering-scottish-elections-john-swinney-snp)

Was the ‘failure/delay’ to act on the Easter warnings the same tactical thinking that a few years later, made Netanyahu (according to Haaretz) refrain from communicating the warnings from the UAE about the Hamas attack of October 7th?

The upside down

Douglas Devananda was in his early 20s when he was first detained at the CID’s headquarters on the infamous Fourth Floor in the early 1980s. 

Having come into the democratic national mainstream under President Premadasa and Minister Ranjan Wijeratne, survived almost a dozen LTTE attacks (one which required brain surgery, and couldn’t prevent near-blindness in one eye), held the strategically vital islands off Jaffna for and with the Sri Lankan State, become a Cabinet Minister, and delivered a speech advocating implementation of the 13th amendment at the 50th anniversary commemoration of the SLFP led by President Chandrika Kumaratunga, he  was back in jail in 2026 and then summoned for questioning to the Fourth Floor by the CID the other day, 45 years after he had first been there in his teens. (https://www.jaffnamonitor.com/featured/cid-questions-douglas-devananda-over-azad-maulanas-account/)

That’s the tragic cycle of the true anti-fascist hero in ‘the Upside Down’ i.e., present day Sri Lanka after two years of rule by AKD-JVP-NPP.

Cool new patriotism

I am glad that the response to Maitreyi Ramakrishnan ‘from Tamil Eelam’ whose far more serious transgression is to publicly accuse Sri Lanka of ‘genocide’, has not been limited to the Sinhala ultranationalists whose discordant discourse turns everybody off. 

I draw the readers’ attention to two young voices, representing a post-Aragalaya discourse. 

I don’t know the name of this young lady, but she and her partner post under the tag ChrisnCrys. Hers is the perfect postwar non-racist response to the ‘Tamil Eelam/Genocide’ discourse: “So tired of this discourse. It’s 2026. Let’s move forward.” (https://www.facebook.com/reel/1226928786316887)

title: Key thing is to create public trust:  SLC Transformation Committee Chairman | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 1 October 2026 00:20

SLC Transformation Committee Chairman Eran Wickramaratne (centre) displays the gazetted Sri Lanka Cricket Bill which is now a public document in the presence of Transformation Committee members Upul Kumarapperuma, PC (left) and Dinal Phillips, PC at the media conference held at SLC headquarters yesterday

By Sa’adi Thawfeeq

Sri Lanka Cricket Transformation Committee Chairman Eran Wickramaratne said that the key thing for the committee apart from drawing up a new constitution was to try and create a public trust.

“Over a period of time the public trust has been broken down,” said Wickramaratne at the monthly meeting with the media to update on the progress made by the Transformation Committee.

“We have to show proper stewardship because we are talking about a national asset here worth Rs. 16 billion. We are looking at independent and professional governance. In the next few weeks and months we will focus more and more on that.”

“We are also looking at financial accountability and close scrutiny by the Attorney-General and transparency and openness which Sri Lanka Cricket will be subjected to and the right to information act. We will be putting those things very much in place.”

Wickramaratne said that he was confident that the national team’s performance will improve as well once all these foundational things are put in place. “Even on the cricket side changes will happen. It won’t be a comfortable period.”

Speaking further Wickramaratne said that one of the big issues the country has faced from the cricketing side was the standard of cricket pitches.   

“They have been very poor. This is very critical in raising the standard of the cricketers and the standard of the game. We have started a process and got a national curator and are doing an independent review. Andy Atkinson, former head curator of ICC is the one who is actually leading the way. We are getting lots of curators who are directly being employed by SLC,” said Wickramaratne.

“The other area where we have started is raising the standard of coaching. It’s not a numbers game, coaching is really a quality issue that has been identified following the strict stringent interview process with the participation of globally acclaimed coach developer Ashley Ross. A new group of district and provincial coaches have been appointed. With the leadership of Ross we are also totally reviewing the High Performance Centre.”

In terms of sports medicine and player welfare Wickramaratne said that Dr. Alex Kountouris, who was the Sri Lankan team’s physio when they won the Cricket World Cup in 1996 was leading the way ‘on what needs to be done’.

A sports psychologist has also been brought in to strengthen the mental skills of the players.

In the umpiring and match refereeing areas, to raise the standards Lyndon Hannibal and Ruchira Palliyaguruge both from the ICC International Umpiring panels were appointed as umpire coach and umpire development manager focusing more on quality.

Athletic Bilbao’s Nico Williams scored the fourth with a crisp dribble and finish.

summary:
Thursday, 1 October 2026 00:00

Sri Lanka Rugby’s Disciplinary Committee has concluded inquiries into two incidents connected with the ongoing Under-19 Next XV National Selection Tournament, following hearings held two days ago, and has imposed disciplinary sanctions on those found responsible.

The first case involved Galle Lions mentor Omalka Gunaratne, who admitted to a charge of physical assault. The Disciplinary Committee found Gunaratne guilty, stating that his conduct brought the game into disrepute and was contrary to the spirit and values of rugby. The Committee also noted that the bodily harm caused by the incident may constitute a criminal offence.

Gunaratne has been handed an immediate three-month suspension from all rugby-related activities falling under SLR and the Sri Lanka Schools Rugby Football Association. The suspension covers coaching, mentoring and playing. In addition, he has received a further one-year suspension, which has been suspended for two years. This additional sanction will come into effect if he is found guilty of any further disciplinary offence during that two-year period.

The other inquiry concerned Kandy Tuskers player Achintha Jayasena and members of the team’s coaching staff, following a complaint submitted by the Isipathana College Rugby Management and Development Committee regarding one of its players. The Committee found Jayasena guilty of misconduct towards a fellow player, causing humiliation and mental distress and disrespecting the player’s dignity.

Jayasena has consequently been removed from the Kandy Tuskers squad for the remainder of the Next XV U-19 National Selection Tournament. Until the tournament concludes, he is prohibited from attending or associating with the team during training, on match days or at events organised by the Kandy Tuskers or Sri Lanka Rugby. Even before these sanctions, Kandy Tuskers management had removed Achintha Jayasena from the team’s final two matches. Jayasena has been instructed to provide a formal apology to the affected player before 5 October 2026.

The Committee further found Kandy Tuskers coaches Lasith Attanagoda and Fazil Marija guilty of failing in their duty of care. The Committee stated that they failed to report the incident through the proper chain of command and attempted to trivialise the abuse by asking the parties to settle the matter.

Both coaches have been fined 20 percent of their respective Next XV U-19 National Selection Tournament contract fees, payable to Sri Lanka Rugby on or before 15 October. All parties have the right to appeal the decisions in writing within seven days of receiving the respective rulings. (SJ)
